column2: MAE-ST dependency manifest -- target: Linux aarch64, NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark), CUDA 12.8 wheels
One conda environment for both repositories: mae_st_lcad main (the model and
data code, imported as the package `mae_st`) and this tooling. Read and
executed by conda.sh, which lives next to this file; README.md explains every
column and how to write a manifest for another machine. Lines starting with
'#' are comments; lines starting with '#!' are metadata parsed by the script.
To target a different machine: copy this file to deps.<platform>.tsv, edit the
#!target line and the affected rows, then run ./conda.sh deps.<platform>.tsv.
No change to conda.sh should ever be needed to support a new machine.
COLUMNS: stage, package, version, arch, installer, source, flags, required, note
stage      install order; rows of one stage sharing installer+source+flags+
required are merged into ONE command (torch + torchvision resolve
together)
version    'latest' | exact | range; ignored for direct=, git=, local=
arch       platform the row was VALIDATED on; documentation, not a filter
source     pip: pypi | index=<url> | extra=<url> | links=<url> | direct=<url>
| git=<url>@<ref> | local=<path>; conda: channel=<a>[,<b>] |
nodefaults  (';'-separated)
required   'yes' aborts on failure, 'no' warns and continues
Versions are the ones of the environment validated on 2026-08-13 (torch,
torchvision and the CUDA stack they pin; a real GPU matmul and Conv3d).
Rows marked "not yet validated" were added afterwards: pin them from the
lock of the first install that has them (README step 12).
cuda= is the newest runtime the DRIVER supports, as nvidia-smi prints it.
The validation ran on driver 595.71.05 (CUDA 13.2); the reference machine
ran driver 580.173.02 on 2026-10-15, hence 13.0 here [to confirm with
nvidia-smi]. The cu128 wheels need a driver >= 570 and compile nothing, so
either works.

column2: pip
column9: Old pip mis-resolves manylinux_2_28_aarch64 tags and silently falls back to building sdists.

column2: setuptools
column9: setuptools >= 81 dropped pkg_resources, which old sdists import; torch 2.11 requires < 82.

column2: wheel
column9: Needed to build any sdist with --no-build-isolation.

column2: torch
column9: The '+cu128' version AND the index are both load-bearing: torch 2.11.0 from PyPI is another binary. conda's pytorch-cuda does not exist for linux-aarch64. Its arch list stops at sm_120, which runs on sm_121 by CUDA minor-version binary compatibility (verify reports it). Pins the whole CUDA stack (cuda-toolkit, cudnn, nccl) with exact ==.

column2: torchvision
column9: Requires torch==2.11.0 exactly; same command as torch so pip resolves the pair together. torchaudio omitted: nothing imports it.

column2: numpy
column9: Pinned from the lock. Torch wheels are built against a numpy ABI that torch does not declare, so a numpy change is a re-validation.

column2: timm
column9: DO NOT BUMP. util/video_vit.py and models_mae.py import timm.models.layers (moved to timm.layers in 0.9) and subclass Attention passing qk_scale (removed in 0.9). py3-none-any, no arch risk.

column2: av
column9: PyAV: decodes the videos (util/decoder) and writes the visualizations (custom/viz_hooks.py). Ships manylinux_2_28_aarch64 wheels with ffmpeg and libx264 bundled.

column2: opencv-python-headless
column9: util/decoder/utils.py and transform.py import cv2 at module level. Headless avoids a Qt stack on a server. OpenCV 5.x requires numpy >= 2.

column2: DELIBERATE OMISSIONS
pytorchvideo, detectron2, torchaudio, decord, slowfast, fairscale, hydra,
fvcore, yacs, scipy, pandas, youtube-dl/yt-dlp: imported nowhere on the
training path of mae_st_lcad main or the tooling (some came from older
environments of this project, pytorchvideo from code main no longer has).
scikit-learn: only main_test's multi-label mAP imports it, lazily.
A CUDA toolkit inside the env: nothing here compiles CUDA code; the torch
wheel ships its runtime.
The repositories themselves: neither is a pip package. The tooling's
bootstrapper registers the mae_st clone as the package `mae_st` at import.
WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT PIN
About twenty pure-Python transitives: tensorboard's (absl-py, grpcio,
markdown, protobuf, werkzeug), matplotlib's (contourpy, fonttools,
kiwisolver, cycler, pyparsing, python-dateutil), torch's soft ones (sympy,
networkx, jinja2, fsspec, filelock, typing-extensions), iopath's
(portalocker, tqdm) and wandb's. Closing that needs a constraints file
(pip install -c), a mechanism not adopted; see DESIGN.md.
